description: holon-coherence has no check that rejects attribution trailers in commit messages (Co-Authored-By, Co-Developed-By, Generated-By, Assisted-By, or a 'Generated with Claude Code' line). The project rule is that no commit carries such a trailer, but nothing enforces it.
goal: Add scripts/check_commit_trailers.py with a pure function find_attribution_lines(message) returning the offending lines (case-insensitive match on lines starting, after optional whitespace, with co-authored-by, co-developed-by, generated-by, assisted-by or 'generated with [claude code'; lines starting with '#' are comment lines and ignored), a --message-file mode that checks one commit message file, and a --range mode that checks every commit in a git revision range; both print each offence with the commit or file and exit non-zero when any exists. Add a git commit-msg hook .githooks/commit-msg that runs the script on the message file, and a new workflow .github/workflows/test-commit-trailers.yml that runs on pull_request with a full-history checkout and runs the script with --range over the pull request's commits (base sha to head sha). Do not edit any existing workflow or the workflows README. Code is self-explaining: no docstrings and no comments except '# why:' comments that record a reason the code cannot show.
rationale: An invariant nothing checks slips through. A hook plus a CI check over the pull request's commits catch it whether or not the author ran hooks.
acceptance_criteria: `commit-msg` hook in the harness and both target repos rejecting the trailer; the same check in CI over the PR's commits (catches commits made without hooks): tests/test_check_commit_trailers.py runs scripts/check_commit_trailers.py --message-file on a real violating message ('feat: x', a blank line, 'Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>') and asserts a non-zero exit and the offending line on stderr; the same message in lower case and a 'Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)' line also fail; a clean message with 'Action-Origin: pr_review' and 'Review-Iteration: 2' trailers exits 0.

The same test file builds a temporary git repository with one clean commit and one commit carrying a Co-Authored-By trailer and asserts --range over both fails naming only the offending commit's short sha, while --range over the clean commit alone exits 0.

The same test file asserts .githooks/commit-msg is executable and invokes scripts/check_commit_trailers.py with --message-file, and that .github/workflows/test-commit-trailers.yml runs on pull_request and calls the script with --range.
`commit-msg` hook in the harness and both target repos rejecting the trailer; the same check in CI over the PR's commits (catches commits made without hooks).
The flow engine's own commits pass the check (test).
The check runs automatically (pre-commit hook and/or CI, and the flow gate where it applies); no agent has to remember it.
The check is proven to fail on a real or reconstructed violation (a test with today's evidence) before it is trusted, and passes on the cleaned state.
Self-explaining code invariant in anything written: no docstrings, no comments except `# why:`.
Target-repository work goes through `holon flow`; the intent never names harness paths or bean ids.

The commits written by this repository's own tooling pass the check: a test in tests/test_check_commit_trailers.py asserts find_attribution_lines returns nothing for the commit messages this repository's scripts generate, if any, and for a representative message ending in 'Action-Origin' and 'Review-Iteration' trailers.
